Two findings — the second is the real blocker.

## 1. The job never reached Netlify

The build succeeded (4.3 GB, 41,588 pages, 120,415 files, ~2h07m). It died in the **Check site shape** step:

```
sort: write failed: 'standard output': Broken pipe
##[error]Process completed with exit code 2
```

`find ... | sort -rn | head -1` — `head` closes the pipe, `sort` gets SIGPIPE, and `set -o pipefail` turns that into a failed step. Pure shell bug, nothing to do with Netlify. Fixed in [.github/workflows/docs.yml](.github/workflows/docs.yml#L259-L272) by replacing `sort | head` with a single-pass `awk` max (also uses `-exec ... {} +` batching, so it's much faster than the 37s per-`find`-exec version). Verified locally: exits 0.

## 2. The site actually exceeds Netlify's per-directory limit

Running the fixed check against your local dist:

```
largest directory: 77915 ./assets
```

Netlify caps a single directory at **54,000 files**. So once the shape check runs correctly, it will fail — correctly — and the deploy still won't happen. VitePress emits one chunk per page into a flat `assets/`, and at 41.5k pages × locales you're ~44% over.

There's no `build.rolldownOptions.output` config in [docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts#L735) — assets go to the flat default. The fix is to shard `assets/` into subdirectories via `chunkFileNames`/`assetFileNames` functions (e.g. bucket by a hash of the chunk name → ~36 shards of ~2.2k files each).

## On seeding locally

I'd skip it. The seed idea assumed Netlify was rejecting the upload; it never got one byte. And a local seed would mean a ~2h full build plus a 4.3 GB upload over your home connection — slower than the runner, with no benefit, and it can't succeed until the `assets/` sharding lands anyway. Your local dist is also only 1.2 GB (stale/partial), so it isn't a valid seed source as-is.

**Recommendation:** land the shape-check fix plus `assets/` sharding on this branch, merge, and let the workflow do the first real seed. The tradeoff is one more ~2h CI cycle to find out if sharding worked; seeding locally would give you a faster feedback loop on the upload step specifically, at the cost of a long local build and a big upload.

Found and fixed it. ## Root cause `vitepress-plugin-llms` was wrapped in [docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts) with: ```ts apply: (config) => !config?.build?.ssr ``` The comment justifying it said the plugin "only ever *emits* files on the client pass." That premise was wrong. Its `transform` also **injects content** into every page: ```js const hintBlock = `
${llmHint}
`; ``` So the client build's markdown carried that hidden "Are you an LLM?" div and the SSR build's did not. Vue hydrated against server markup with exactly one child too few, walked off the end, and threw `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodeType')`. That also explains every observation that had me chasing locale scoping earlier: non-root locales were clean **only** because the plugin's `ignoreFiles` already excluded `/**`, so both passes agreed there. The bug was English-only for a reason that had nothing to do with locales. ## How I tracked it Building with `define: { __VUE_PROD_HYDRATION_MISMATCH_DETAILS__: "true" }` was the unlock — production Vue reports the crash with no context otherwise. That surfaced `Server rendered element contains fewer child nodes than client vdom`, and resolving the console argument's node handle printed the offending element verbatim, hint div and all. ## Result Page sweep before and after, same build config: | Page | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `/` | mismatch warning | clean | | `/api/` | **crash** | clean | | `/guide/getting-started` | **crash** | clean | | `/guide/packages`, `/guide/plugins`, `/api/css/`, `/guide/cdn`, `/guide/components`, `/guide/generated-output` | **crash** | clean | | `/guide/architecture` | **crash** | mismatch warning | llms output is unaffected: `llms.txt` (68 KB, 893 links, no duplicates) and `llms-full.txt` (1.4 MB) still generate once, and the hint div now appears exactly once in the SSR HTML. Full suite: 2,175 tests pass, coverage unchanged (statements 94.16%, lines 95.36%). `vp check` and markdown lint clean. ## One thing left, deliberately `/guide/architecture` still logs `Hydration completed but contains mismatches` — no crash, page renders fine. That's a **different** root cause: the mermaid component's watcher runs `immediate`, so `renderDiagram` replaces the diagram's innerHTML with SVG while Vue is still hydrating. It's a separate bug in a separate component, so I didn't fold it into this fix. Say the word and I'll take it. I also logged the gotcha in [docs/engineering-log.md](docs/engineering-log.md) with the durable rule — never gate a content-injecting plugin to one VitePress pass — plus the diagnostic define, since that's the part that turns a 30-minute hunt into a 2-minute one. Changeset added.
